Goal & deliverables (8–10 weeks): produce a consolidated methods report (v0 stress‑test protocol + top‑10 mis‑spec categories), a compact mixed‑domain benchmark (~100 cases) with two‑tier annotations (shallow labels for all, deep annotations for ~25 priority cases), a monitoring prototype (streaming ingestion + near‑miss detector + lightweight dashboard mock‑up), two instrumented demos (customer‑support and sandboxed AI nurse) with logs and failure‑attribution dossiers, and a 2–3 page regulatory brief + slide pack describing capabilities and limitations.  
Weeks 1–2: finalize the v0 protocol and annotation guidelines, lock the 100‑case slice and priority deep‑annotation list, define a pragmatic logging/monitoring schema mapped to the regulator’s examples, allocate the supplemental engineer to end‑to‑end monitoring integration, and trigger any needed ethics/review steps for the AI nurse sandbox.  
Weeks 2–5: run stress tests across 2–3 model families on the compact slice, collect instrumented logs from both demos, run the near‑miss detector offline to tune signal heuristics, and rework logging granularity where needed (systems should budget ~30–40% early effort on logging/tagging to be credible).  
Weeks 5–8: deploy the monitoring prototype in sandboxed mode (simulated continuous ingestion), produce dashboard mockups that surface top near‑miss categories, signal rates, and representative transcripts, run simulated continuous monitoring to measure alert precision/recall and false‑positive load, and execute targeted ablations and interpretability probes tied to observed failures.  
Weeks 8–10: finalize the methods appendix and benchmark with baseline metrics, assemble two demo annexes (scripts, logs, near‑miss examples, mitigation experiments), produce the regulatory brief + slide pack for the roundtable (with a clear limitations/assumptions section), and confirm remaining resourcing/annotation tradeoffs and approvals for release.
